question: Using only elementary row transformations, reduce the matrix $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\0&1&3\\0&0&2\end{bmatrix}$$ to the identity matrix of order $3$, showing the effect of each successive transformation.
explanation:
Applying Elementary Row Transformations

We start with $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\0&1&3\\0&0&2\end{bmatrix}$$ First apply $R_3\to\frac{1}{2}R_3$. Then $$A\to\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\0&1&3\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Next apply $R_2\to R_2-3R_3$. This gives $$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Now apply $R_1\to R_1+R_3$, obtaining $$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Finally, apply $R_1\to R_1-2R_2$. We obtain $$\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}=I_3$$ Each transformation is an elementary row operation involving multiplication of a row by a non-zero scalar or addition of a scalar multiple of one row to another. Hence, the given matrix is transformed into the identity matrix $I_3$.
